newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to down 0.05.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar called to open flat to down 0.05.

text.p: CSCE world sugar was called to open unchanged to 0.05 cent weaker Tuesday, dealers said.

The market is expected to hold to its recent trading range ahead of the expiry of the spot July contract on June 30. Following heavy liquidation last week, the expiry should remain orderly, traders said.
Monday, the July contract closed 0.07 cent firmer at 11.13 cents a lb, traded 11.23 to 11.02 cents. October ended up 0.08 cent at 11.11 cents, while the rest 0.07 to 0.01 cent higher.
An estimated 33,434 lots changed hands on the day.

India said it will release 750,000 tonnes of free sale sugar in each of the months of July, August and September. The 2.25 million tonne release, for domestic consumption only, comes in addition to the 369,000 tonnes of levy sugar quota that will also be released in each of those months, India's Food Ministry said in a statement.
LIFFE white sugar futures were trading slightly weaker, with the spot August contract down $0.30 to $318.80, at 0840 EDT/1240 GMT. The rest of the board stood $1.30 lower to $0.40 higher.
